items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: On J.J.’s last album, on the brass orchestra, Slide Hampton called me up. I was playing baritone horn.

ctx.x: Right. But I guess that’s part of the gig is to know the basic repertoire.

Know the repertoire, know how to play, know how to read, know how to divide notes and all of that, and how to balance and blend at the first reading. I never did. I never got music in advance. Well once or twice I did. On J.J.’s last album, on the brass orchestra, Slide Hampton called me up. I was playing baritone horn. Bruce Bonvusato and myself played baritones and they had trombones and horns and all the rest. But Slide called and he said, “Would you mind coming up to the apartment, I’d like to show you these…
Yeah, he writes some challenging music.
